image_description: A full-body shot of a large, dark greyish-green iguana resting on a paved or gravel surface. The iguana is positioned diagonally with its head raised and facing right. It features a prominent dorsal crest running down its spine, a visible dewlap under the chin, and a long, banded tail extending to the left. The background consists of blurred green foliage.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is large and triangular with a prominent dewlap (loose skin fold) hanging from the throat.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head shape is clearly triangular and robust. A distinct fold of skin (dewlap) is visible hanging from the throat area, consistent with the species description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Eyes are large with round pupils and golden irises.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: While the eye socket is visible, the resolution and lighting angle prevent clear verification of the pupil shape (round vs slit) and the specific iris color (golden). It appears dark due to shadow/reflection.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: A large circular subtympanic shield (scale) is present below the tympanum.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: A large, distinct circular scale pattern is visible on the side of the head, located posterior to the jawline, matching the location and description of the subtympanic shield.
The torso appears thick and muscular, fitting the 'robust' description for an adult iguana.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Coloration is bright green in juveniles, becoming darker green to greyish-green in adults with broad black bands on the body and tail.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The iguana exhibits a dark greyish-green coloration typical of adults. Distinct dark banding is clearly visible on the tail and faintly on the body.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Row of enlarged, spine-like scales running from the nape along the midline of the back to the tail base, forming a serrated crest.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: A continuous, serrated row of spines is clearly visible running from the neck down the spine. This is the most defining feature and is perfectly rendered.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is covered in small, granular scales with larger, plate-like scales on the head.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The texture on the body appears pebbled/granular, while the scales on the snout and cheek area appear larger and more plate-like, consistent with reptile anatomy.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Limbs are long and muscular with five clawed digits on each foot.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The front right limb is clearly visible, showing muscular definition and long toes with claws. The rear right limb is also visible. While not all 5 digits on every foot are individually countable due to angle/occlusion, the visible anatomy is structurally correct and shows no signs of fusion or missing parts.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is laterally compressed and longer than body, used for balance and defense.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is visibly long (extending beyond the frame relative to the body mass) and has the characteristic ringed/banded appearance. Lateral compression is implied by the profile view.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific species classification (Iguana iguana) and rule out look-alike lizards.
To verify the structural integrity of the limbs and spine alignment, ensuring no extra limbs or skeletal warping.
To check for edge bleeding between the complex dorsal crest/spines and the background foliage.
To assess overall texture consistency of the scales and ground surface.

focus_areas: Dorsal crest continuity and connection to the spine
Digit count and separation on visible feet
Texture transition between granular body scales and plate-like head scales
Edge sharpness of the tail against the gravel background
